newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Hamas wins professional poll in Gaza.
newsitem.headline: Hamas wins professional poll in Gaza.

text.p: Supporters of the militant Islamic Resistance Movement Hamas swept elections for the Engineering Association of Gaza and Hamas's co-founder now heads the group, association officials said on Saturday.
They said Hamas won eight seats, Palestinian President Yasser Arafat's mainstream PLO Fatah faction took two seats and one seat was won by an independent in the Friday poll.
Palestinians said the results reflected frustration with peace moves plunged into crisis this month by Israel breaking ground on a new Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem.
Days after the groundbreaking, an Islamist suicide bomber killed three Israelis in Tel Aviv on March 21. A caller to Israeli police claimed Hamas was responsible for the attack.

Ismail Abu Shanab, who founded Hamas with Sheikh Ahmed Yassin in the 1980s and was released by Israel from prison several months ago after serving an eight-year sentence for Hamas affiliation, was now association chairman.
"Many people are frustrated with the peace deal and disappointed at the Palestinians' situation," a Fatah member of the association said.
Pundits had expected Fatah would make a better showing.
In the last poll in 1993, seats on the group's board were split equally between Hamas and Fatah.
Arafat signed an interim peace deal with Israel in 1993 that provided limited Palestinian self-rule in much of Gaza and parts of the West Bank. Arafat's headquarters have been in Gaza since 1994.
Hamas opposed the peace deal. Its militants have killed scores of Israelis in attacks aimed at torpedoing it. Hamas has long had strong support in Gaza.
